73.78200,18.58865.name: Atharva Nursing Home
73.78200,18.58865.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-84.29329,33.88084.name: High-Containment Continuity Laboratory (HCCL)
-84.29329,33.88084.state: Atlanta, GA 75D301-18-R-67933 (CDC Roybal Campus), United States
-84.29329,33.88084.company: Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
-84.29329,33.88084.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, under construction. Run by Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-102.55000,23.63000.name: Mexico — no public clinic register
-102.55000,23.63000.desc: A significant destination for cross-border treatment, regulated at state level with no national register.

-75.69720,45.42150.name: Canadian Food Inspection Agency — PNT decisions
-75.69720,45.42150.desc: Canada regulates by what a plant is rather than by how it was made, assessing anything with a novel trait whatever the method. Transgenic events and products of mutagenesis or editing sit in the same public register, which makes Canada the one country where the second group stays visible instead of disappearing into a carve-out. The register is also where the gap shows: the deregulated class carries no international identifier, so it cannot be tracked across borders.

-46.68200,-23.58600.name: JBS
-46.68200,-23.58600.state: São Paulo — Av. Marginal Direita do Tietê 500
-46.68200,-23.58600.desc: The largest meat processor in the world, buying livestock across several continents. Its purchasing standards function as private regulation for everything upstream — which cloned or edited animals are acceptable, which feed is, which traceability is required — decided commercially and applied across more producers than most national rules reach.

7.59300,47.56800.name: Novartis — Zolgensma outcomes-based agreements
7.59300,47.56800.desc: Zolgensma is a one-time gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy priced above two million dollars, sold in some countries under contracts where the payer pays less if the child does not improve. Paying for a result rather than a product is a new arrangement in medicine, and it exists because a single-dose cure breaks the instalment logic every health system was built on.

-70.61000,-33.42000.name: BioSigma
-70.61000,-33.42000.desc: A joint venture of Codelco, the Chilean state copper company, and JX Nippon, using engineered bacteria to leach copper from ore too poor to smelt. Bioleaching puts living organisms into mine waste at industrial scale, in a setting governed by mining law rather than by biosafety law.
